ADU, In-Law Suite & Extended Family Residence Contractors in Tampa Bay

Room for multigenerational living

More Tampa Bay families are looking for a way to keep parents, adult children or long-term guests close while giving everyone their own space. Depending on the property, that can mean an attached in-law suite with its own entrance, a converted garage, or a separate accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on the same lot. Local land development codes in the Tampa Bay area use different names for these spaces — accessory dwelling unit, guest house, accessory living space or extended family residence — and each jurisdiction sets its own rules.

That is why every project begins with a feasibility review of your specific property. Before design is finalized, we look at zoning, setbacks, lot coverage, flood-zone status, utility connections and any HOA or deed restrictions, and we confirm which approvals the applicable authority — such as Hillsborough County, the City of Tampa, Pinellas County or the City of Clearwater — requires for the type of unit you want to build.

From there, Unique Building Contractors manages the project as the Florida Certified Building Contractor of record (CBC1268844): coordinating plans with the architect or designer and engineers, submitting permit applications, building the foundation, structure and building systems, and scheduling every required inspection through final approval. The goal is a private, comfortable living space that fits the main home and meets Florida Building Code requirements for wind, flood and energy.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between an ADU, an in-law suite and an extended family residence?

An in-law suite is usually an attached part of the main home with its own bedroom, bathroom and living area. An accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a separate, self-contained living unit — attached or detached — on the same lot. "Extended family residence" is a term some local land development codes use for living space intended for family members. Which option is allowed, and how it is defined, depends on your jurisdiction and zoning.

Can I build an ADU or in-law suite on my property in Tampa Bay?

It depends on the property. Zoning district, lot size, setbacks, lot coverage, flood zone, utilities and HOA or deed restrictions all affect what can be built. We review these items for your address and confirm requirements with the applicable county or city before design is finalized.

Should the unit be attached or detached?

Attached in-law suites can share the home's structure and systems and may be simpler where the lot is tight. Detached ADUs offer more privacy but need their own foundation, utility connections and setbacks. We compare both options for your lot, budget priorities and household needs during planning.

Do ADUs and in-law suites require permits?

Yes. New living space requires building permits covering structural, electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, and some jurisdictions require additional zoning or land-use approval. Unique Building Contractors prepares and submits permit applications and manages every required inspection as the licensed contractor of record (CBC1268844).

How much does an ADU or in-law suite cost?

Cost depends on size, attached versus detached construction, site work, utility connections, finishes and permit requirements. We provide a project-specific estimate after reviewing the property and defining the scope — call (813) 523-7828 to schedule a free estimate.

Can a garage be converted into an in-law suite?

Often, yes. A garage conversion can create a bedroom, bathroom and living area, but it requires review of parking requirements, floor elevation, insulation, windows and egress, and the needed permits. We evaluate whether your garage is a good candidate before design begins.
